question.text: If \(\sin \theta\) and \(\cos \theta\) are the roots of the equation \(a x^2-b x+c=0\), then \(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}\) and \(\mathrm{c}\) satisfy the relation

solution.text:
Hints: \(\sin \theta+\cos \theta=\frac{b}{a}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta=\frac{c}{a} \\
& \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^2=1+\frac{2 c}{a} \\
& b^2=a^2+2 a c \\
& a^2-b^2+2 a c=0
\end{aligned}\)
